rows.text: Excessive words are not necessary here, young one. Prepare to tread forth into the river of knowledge.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: Come. I shall bestow upon you the greatest treasure of the Grove.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: Hey! Watch your tongue, young one.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: Alas, there's no wealth to be here, though there is something much more precious — knowledge.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: I am a strand of consciousness left behind by the Great Sage Calidorthos to manage this grand library, known as the Index.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: Y—You! Hiss... I shall graciously overlook your foolishness, considering there is yet room for your education.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: Corrupted by the black tide, the underground network is slowly decaying. What remains is nothing more than scattered remnants of certain scrolls.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: Before you can refuse, a blinding radiance soaks into your thoughts, encompassing your soul essence into the labyrinthine root system.
Indeed, I was not mistaken in my judgment. It is but a mere shard drawn from memory's depths, yet it bears the majesty of an astral vessel, akin to the tyrant's fabled skyship.
rows.speaker: Calidorthos

rows.text: You even find yourself doubting whether a simulated Screwllum or Herta might appear in the next moment.
As long as the program works, it doesn't matter whether these three old variables can be formulaically used to unlock the Titans' secrets. We shouldn't get caught up in the details.
Maybe like how a protagonist must have a baseball bat, the Divergent Universe is much more compatible with {TEXTJOIN#87} even if it's a simulation.
It's Cerces's wisdom, my dear friend.
It's fine. He'll be overjoyed when you bring the memories you made here to him.
